standard.title: Diversity of First Nations media arts
standard.description: investigate the diversity of First Nations Australians' media arts works and practices, considering culturally responsive approaches to Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property rights
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have some awareness that First Nations Australians have media arts practices. They have not yet investigated this diversity systematically or engaged with ICIP rights frameworks in media arts contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate the diversity of First Nations Australian media arts with genuine cultural responsiveness, understanding and applying ICIP rights frameworks.

nodes.label: Understanding ICIP rights in media arts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain what ICIP rights mean in media arts contexts and describe what culturally responsive engagement looks like in practice
nodes.minimum_width: Explain what ICIP rights are in a media arts context; give one example of what respectful engagement with First Nations media arts looks like
nodes.typical_width: Investigate ICIP rights frameworks and explain how they apply to media arts practice — using cultural images, sounds or stories in works, distributing works that feature cultural content
wider: Investigate a specific case of cultural appropriation in media arts where ICIP rights were denied — explain what happened and what a respectful alternative would have looked like
Collaboratively construct guidelines for safe, ethical, legal and responsible media use — develop criteria for deciding whether ideas from existing cultural expressions can be used in new work
Investigate issues relating to use of First Nations languages or stories in screen-based works — analyse specific case studies illustrating ICIP protocols

response_modes.reason: Students commonly understand ICIP rights abstractly without being able to reason through specific media arts scenarios — knowing permission is needed without working out who to ask, what counts as cultural expression in media, or what responsible practice looks like. Scenario-based scaffolding builds actionable understanding rather than declarative awareness.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The collaborative guideline construction direction is uniquely rich in media arts — students produce an actual working document that could guide real production decisions, connecting ethical reasoning to practical media-making. The case study investigation direction also opens genuine critical territory about how media industries have misused cultural content.
success_criteria: Explains what ICIP rights mean in a media arts context
Gives at least one specific example of respectful engagement
Does not reduce ICIP to a checklist — explains the reasoning behind protocols

nodes.label: Investigating First Nations Australian media arts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate the diversity of First Nations Australian media arts works and practices with cultural responsiveness
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate at least one First Nations Australian media arts work or practitioner in depth; explain what makes it culturally significant and how ICIP principles are evident
nodes.typical_width: Investigate diverse First Nations Australian media arts works and practices; analyse choices artists make about technical elements, story principles and audience relationships; explain how ICIP principles shape those choices
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australian media artists construct representations of resilience in response to colonisation — analyse how technical and symbolic choices serve that communicative purpose
Investigate how First Nations Australian media arts works use story principles that may differ from dominant Western narrative structures — analyse what those differences communicate
Research how to select and use historical materials that accurately communicate First Nations perspectives — develop own criteria for responsible use in media arts practice

response_modes.reason: Students commonly treat First Nations Australian media arts as a single tradition rather than understanding the diversity across hundreds of distinct cultural groups and a wide range of contemporary media forms. Multiple distinct investigation contexts — different practitioners, forms, and thematic focuses — resolve this misconception through genuine breadth.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The story principles direction is particularly rich — many First Nations Australian media works use non-linear, circular or relational narrative structures that challenge the dominant Western story model. Advancing students who investigate this develop both cultural understanding and expanded production possibilities for own work.
success_criteria: Investigates at least one First Nations Australian media work in genuine depth
Explains cultural significance — not just describes content

nodes.label: Applying culturally responsive approaches in media arts
nodes.checkpoint: Students can make ethical choices about how they engage with First Nations Australian cultural material in media arts, applying ICIP protocols in production and distribution decisions.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least one ICIP protocol question to own media arts practice; explain the reasoning behind the protocol.
nodes.typical_width: Apply multiple protocol questions to own practice across production and distribution; explain how the protocols guide ethical engagement with First Nations Australian cultural material in media arts.
wider: Collaboratively construct guidelines for safe, ethical, legal and responsible use of First Nations Australian cultural material in media arts — develop criteria for deciding whether ideas from existing cultural expressions can be used.
Evaluate a specific case where ICIP rights were denied in media arts — analyse what happened and what a respectful alternative would have looked like.
success_criteria: Applies at least one ICIP protocol question to a real or hypothetical media arts practice scenario
Explains the ethical reasoning behind the protocol

response_modes.reason: Applying ICIP protocols in media arts requires reasoning through specific production decisions — what content is being used, who owns it, what permission is needed.
